question.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Trigonometric Functions Using the Product or Quotient Rule
question.worked_solution:
Applying the quotient rule, using the formula for the derivative of $\operatorname{arctan}⁡x$ and applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})}{{x}^{6}+1}) \\  & =\frac{({x}^{6}+1)\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3}))-\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{6}+1)}{({x}^{6}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{({x}^{6}+1)\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{6}+1}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3})-\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})\cdot 6{x}^{5}}{({x}^{6}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\frac{({x}^{6}+1)(3{x}^{2})}{{x}^{6}+1}-6{x}^{5}\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})}{({x}^{6}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}-6{x}^{5}\operatorname{arctan}⁡({x}^{3})}{({x}^{6}+1)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$
